use: Informal; a secret, lie or trick coming out.

example.english: Uh oh, my girlfriend found out.

examplePolite.ja: 彼女にバレてしまいました。

notes: The person who finds out takes ni: oya ni bareta (my parents found out).

use: Fooling someone, from a prank to fraud; the passive damasareta (I got tricked) is very common.

example.romaji: Damasareta! Zenbu uso datta n da.
example.ja: だまされた！全部うそだったんだ。
example.english: I got tricked! It was all lies.

examplePolite.romaji: Damasaremashita. Zenbu uso datta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: だまされました。全部うそだったんです。
examplePolite.english: I was tricked. It was all lies.

notes: Telling a lie is uso o tsuku.

english: get caught; get arrested; hold on to
use: Being caught by the police or someone chasing you; also grabbing hold: tsurikawa ni tsukamaru (hold the strap).

example.ja: 犯人、やっと捕まったって。
example.english: I heard they finally caught the guy who did it.

examplePolite.romaji: Hannin ga yatto tsukamatta sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 犯人がやっと捕まったそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear the culprit has finally been caught.

notes: tsukamaeru is 'catch' (someone catches you). Also 'reach someone': kare ni tsukamaranai (I can't get hold of him).

use: For 'had X stolen', use the passive: X o nusumareta.

example.english: Someone stole my wallet on the train!

examplePolite.ja: 電車で財布を盗まれました。
examplePolite.english: My wallet was stolen on the train.

use: Dodging the truth by laughing it off, changing the subject or fudging the numbers.

example.ja: ごまかさないで、ちゃんと答えて。
example.english: Don't dodge it, give me a straight answer.

examplePolite.ja: ごまかさないで、ちゃんと答えてください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't dodge it, give me a straight answer.

notes: warai de gomakasu: laugh it off. Milder than damasu.

use: Getting away from danger or a place, or ducking a hard situation.

example.ja: ここは危ない、早く逃げて！
example.english: It's dangerous here, get out quick!

examplePolite.romaji: Koko wa abunai desu, hayaku nigete kudasai!
examplePolite.ja: ここは危ないです、早く逃げてください！
examplePolite.english: It's dangerous here, please get out quickly!

notes: nigeru na! (don't run away!) is a stock drama line. Also 'avoid facing': genjitsu kara nigeru (run from reality).

use: Mostly heard in crime dramas, and as an angry threat: korosu zo!

example.romaji: Kare wa mushi mo korosenai yo.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare wa mushi mo korosenai hito desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は虫も殺せない人ですよ。
examplePolite.english: He's someone who wouldn't hurt a fly.

notes: Passive korosareru: be killed. Also 'hold back': koe o korosu (keep your voice down).

use: Often passive: X ni makikomareru (get caught up in an accident, a fight, trouble).

example.romaji: Gomen, hen na koto ni makikonjatta.
example.ja: ごめん、変なことに巻き込んじゃった。
example.english: Sorry for dragging you into this mess.

examplePolite.romaji: Sumimasen, hen na koto ni makikonde shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、変なことに巻き込んでしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry for dragging you into this mess.

notes: jiko ni makikomareta: got caught up in an accident.

english: go through (something bad); have a bad time
use: Always after a describing word: hidoi me ni au (have an awful time), abunai me ni au (have a close call).

example.romaji: Kinou hidoi me ni atta yo.
example.ja: 昨日ひどい目に遭ったよ。
example.english: I had an awful time yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou wa hidoi me ni aimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日はひどい目に遭いました。
examplePolite.english: I had an awful time yesterday.

notes: au here is 遭う (run into trouble), not 会う (meet someone).

use: Humble suru for your own actions, almost always as itashimasu in shops and business.

example.ja: こちらで確認いたします。

notes: Set lines: shitsurei itashimasu, yoroshiku onegai itashimasu. Never for what the listener does.

use: Respectful suru for what the listener or a superior does.

example.romaji: Okyakusama, onomimono wa dou nasaimasu ka?
example.ja: お客様、お飲み物はどうなさいますか？
example.english: And what would you like to drink?

notes: The masu form is irregular: nasaimasu. Never about yourself; that's itasu.

use: Handling a customer, problem or situation; common at work and in shops.

examplePolite.romaji: Kore wa dare ga taiou shimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: これは誰が対応しますか？

notes: taiou ga hayai: quick to respond. Also 'supports': eigo taiou (English available).
